name: ReclamationReservoirsLakesandPools
title: Reclamation Reservoirs, Lakes and Pools
description:
This GIS layer represents the spatial extent and key attributes of reservoirs associated with dams owned, operated, or managed by the Bureau of Reclamation. It is part of the Enterprise Asset Registry used to support water resource management, infrastructure planning, and operational decision-making. Each feature in the layer corresponds to a reservoir polygon and includes associated metadata such as reservoir name, associated dam, river system, region, storage capacity, and ownership status. The dataset is maintained by Reclamation’s Asset Management Office and is periodically updated to reflect changes in infrastructure and water management operations.

Reservoir

A reservoir is a body of water impounded by a dam in which water can be stored. For classification purposes, a body of water must store at least 50 acre-feet at the maximum controllable water surface and be associated with a dam to be classified as a reservoir.

Lake

A lake is a body of water that is not primarily associated with a dam but is important for Reclamation mission areas (e.g. water delivery, recreation, etc.). The body of water must store at least 50 ac-ft to be classified as a lake.

Pool

A pool is a body of water impounded by a dam or small water barrier but has a total storage volume of less than 50 ac-ft at the maximum controllable water surface.
snippet: The objective of the Reservoirs Asset Class task is to establish a single authoritative source in GIS format for Reclamation’s entire inventory of natural or man-made water impoundments and implement processes and procedures for maintaining the inventory into the future.
